# Investigating Rate 6

Rate 6 is Eversource's proposed heat-pump rate. In winter (November–March) it charges
less for each kWh above 700 in a month than for the first 700. In April–October every kWh
pays the same rate.

This notebook looks at Eversource homes before and after they switch to a heat pump
(ResStock upgrades 00 and 02). The starting point is each home's bill before the heat
pump, on Rate 1. The notebook compares that with the home's bill after the heat pump
under Rate 6 as filed and two delivery-only variants of Rate 6 (FIXED+RATE=MC and
RATE=MC), each at its 700 kWh winter threshold and with that threshold moved to the
home's own pre-heat-pump usage. Every "bill change from Rate 1" therefore includes both
the switch to a heat pump and the move to the new tariff. The last section measures how
much of the extra electricity from switching to a heat pump falls under and above 700 kWh.

## Load the data

Each bill comes from CAIRO's master bills table: one row per building per month, plus
an `Annual` row. `energy_total_bill` adds electricity, gas, propane, and oil. Electricity
is the fixed charge, delivery, and supply. Every chart is weighted by ResStock's sample
weight, so counts are Eversource households, not ResStock buildings.

```{python}
#| label: load-annual-bills

def annual_bills(segment: str, columns: list[str]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Annual rows for every Eversource building in a segment."""
    return (
        load_master_bills(STATE, BATCH, segment)
        .filter((pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == UTILITY) & (pl.col("month") == "Annual"))
        .select("bldg_id", "weight", "upgrade", *columns)
        .collect()
    )


bills_rate1 = annual_bills(SEG_RATE1_BASE, [BILL_COL])
bills_rate6 = annual_bills(
    SEG_RATE6_HP, [BILL_COL, "elec_fixed_charge", "elec_delivery_bill", "elec_supply_bill"]
)
for label, bills, expected in [("Rate 1", bills_rate1, 0), ("Rate 6", bills_rate6, 2)]:
    upgrades = bills["upgrade"].unique().to_list()
    assert upgrades == [expected], f"{label}: expected upgrade {expected} only, got {upgrades}"
    print(f"{label}: {bills.height:,} buildings, upgrade {upgrades[0]}")
assert set(bills_rate1["bldg_id"]) == set(bills_rate6["bldg_id"])
bills_rate6.head(5)
```

Heating type is the pre-heat-pump classification, `postprocess_group.heating_type_v2`

Monthly grid kWh is CAIRO's `elec_grid_kwh`, the consumption the tariff is applied to.

```{python}
#| label: monthly-grid-kwh

def grid_kwh(segment: str, name: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Monthly grid kWh for every Eversource building."""
    return (
        load_master_bills(STATE, BATCH, segment)
        .filter((pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == UTILITY) & (pl.col("month") != "Annual"))
        .select("bldg_id", "month", pl.col("elec_grid_kwh").alias(name))
        .collect()
    )


monthly_kwh_pair = grid_kwh(SEG_RATE6_BASE, "kwh_before").join(
    grid_kwh(SEG_RATE6_HP, "kwh_after"), on=["bldg_id", "month"], how="inner"
)
assert monthly_kwh_pair.height == bills_rate6.height * 12
monthly_kwh_pair.head(5)
```

## Bills under today's rates

All histograms in this notebook share one x-axis, the 1st to 99th weighted percentile
of every bill set together, so they can be compared at a glance. The subtitle gives each
set's weighted median and mean. The axis is set further down, once every bill set exists.

```{python}
#| label: hist-helper

BIN_WIDTH = 250.0


def weighted_mean(df: pl.DataFrame, col: str) -> float:
    return float((df[col] * df["weight"]).sum() / df["weight"].sum())


def plot_annual_bill_hist(df: pl.DataFrame, title: str) -> plt.ggplot:
    """Weighted histogram of annual energy bills on the shared x-axis window."""
    binned = (
        df.with_columns(
            ((pl.col(BILL_COL) / BIN_WIDTH).floor() * BIN_WIDTH + BIN_WIDTH / 2).alias("bin_center")
        )
        .group_by("bin_center")
        .agg(pl.col("weight").sum().alias("households"))
    )
    lo, hi = X_LIMITS
    breaks_fn = breaks_extended(n=8)
    median = weighted_quantile(df, BILL_COL, 0.5)
    mean = weighted_mean(df, BILL_COL)
    lines = pl.DataFrame({"xintercept": [median, mean], "stat": ["Median", "Mean"]}).with_columns(
        pl.col("stat").cast(pl.Enum(["Median", "Mean"]))
    )
    return (
        plt.ggplot(binned, plt.aes(x="bin_center", y="households"))
        + plt.geom_col(width=BIN_WIDTH * 0.9, fill=SB_COLORS["sky"])
        + plt.geom_vline(lines, plt.aes(xintercept="xintercept", color="stat"), size=0.8)
        + plt.scale_color_manual(
            values={"Median": SB_COLORS["midnight"], "Mean": SB_COLORS["carrot"]}, name=" "
        )
        # coord_cartesian zooms without dropping bills outside the window.
        + plt.coord_cartesian(xlim=(lo, hi))
        + plt.scale_x_continuous(
            breaks=lambda _limits: breaks_fn((lo, hi)),
            labels=lambda xs: [f"${x:,.0f}" for x in xs],
        )
        + plt.scale_y_continuous(labels=lambda ys: [f"{y:,.0f}" for y in ys])
        + plt.labs(
            x="Annual energy bill",
            y="Households (weighted)",
            title=title,
            # Escaped: two bare "$" in one string turn on matplotlib mathtext.
            subtitle=f"Weighted median \\${median:,.0f}, mean \\${mean:,.0f}",
        )
        + theme_switchbox()
        + plt.theme(figure_size=(10.5, 4.5), legend_title=plt.element_blank())
    )


def quadrant_by_heating(df: pl.DataFrame, value_col: str, title: str):
    """One stacked bar per heating type, in the four bill-change colors used across reports."""
    rows = [
        (
            label,
            df.filter(pl.col("heating_label") == label).select(pl.col(value_col).alias("delta"), "weight"),
        )
        for label in HEATING_ORDER
    ]
    return plot_bill_change_quadrant_comparison(rows, title=title)
```

## The tariffs

Rate 6 as filed comes from this batch's `RDP_REF`. The two variants come from
`origin/main` of rate-design-platform at `bdde102b`, and only the delivery JSON of each
is used. Supply is the same flat seasonal commodity on Rate 1, Rate 6, and both
variants, about 11.2 cents per kWh from January through June and 9.7 cents from July
through December, and it does not differ between the two winter blocks. Keeping today's
supply bill and changing only delivery is the whole comparison. The delivery-and-supply
JSON adds that same commodity back in, so it repeats the delivery bill.

- **RATE=MC** keeps the $30.95 customer charge and Block 1, and lowers winter Block 2 to
  marginal cost. The winter discount grows from about 1.9 cents to about 5.3 cents per kWh.
- **FIXED+RATE=MC** does that too, and moves the marginal facilities cost into the
  customer charge, which rises from $30.95 to $57.13. Block 1 falls with it, so the
  winter discount is also about 5.3 cents.

Gas, oil, and propane bills are kept as CAIRO computed them in every case.

```{python}
#| label: load-tariffs

# includes_supply is None for filed Rate 6: its 700 kWh bill is CAIRO's own, not a rebuild.
TARIFFS = {
    "rate6": ("Rate 6", "ct_eversource_rate6", RDP_REF, None),
    "fixed_ratemc": ("FIXED+RATE=MC", "ct_eversource_rate6_fixed_ratemc", TARIFF_REF, False),
    "ratemc": ("RATE=MC", "ct_eversource_rate6_ratemc", TARIFF_REF, False),
}

tariffs: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
for key, (name, stem, ref, includes_supply) in TARIFFS.items():
    tariff = load_tariff_json(STATE, UTILITY, stem, ref)
    rates = month_block_rates(tariff)
    tiered = rates.filter(pl.col("r2").is_not_null())
    tariffs[key] = {
        "name": name,
        "stem": stem,
        "includes_supply": includes_supply,
        "fixed_monthly": float(tariff["fixedchargefirstmeter"]),
        "rates": rates,
        "winter_months": tiered["month"].to_list(),
        "threshold_kwh": tiered["threshold_kwh"].unique().to_list(),
        "block_gaps": (tiered["r1"] - tiered["r2"]).round(5).unique().sort().to_list(),
    }

pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "tariff": [t["name"] for t in tariffs.values()],
        "fixed_monthly": [t["fixed_monthly"] for t in tariffs.values()],
        "winter_months": [", ".join(t["winter_months"]) for t in tariffs.values()],
        "threshold_kwh": [str(t["threshold_kwh"]) for t in tariffs.values()],
        "block_gap": [str(t["block_gaps"]) for t in tariffs.values()],
    }
)
```

### Building the bills

For a variant's 700 kWh bill, each month's energy charge is rebuilt from the upgrade-02
grid kWh: Block 1 up to 700 kWh and Block 2 above it in a two-block winter month, one
rate in a summer month. Add twelve months of the variant's fixed charge, and whatever
part of today's bill the JSON does not replace.

For every tariff, filed Rate 6 included, the personalized bill starts from that tariff's
700 kWh bill and changes only the winter energy charge. For one winter month, let $B$ be
upgrade-00 kWh, $A$ be upgrade-02 kWh, and $r_1$ and $r_2$ the two block rates:

- the 700 kWh tariff charges $r_1 \min(A, 700) + r_2 \max(A - 700, 0)$
- the personalized tariff charges $r_1 \min(A, B) + r_2 \max(A - B, 0)$

Their difference simplifies to

$$(r_2 - r_1)\,\big[\max(A - B, 0) - \max(A - 700, 0)\big]$$

`personalized_block_adjustment` in `lib.rates_analysis.block_rates` is that expression.
If a home's use stayed flat or went down, every winter kWh pays Block 1. Fixed charges
and summer months are the same under both versions.

```{python}
#| label: bill-builders

def energy_charge_at_threshold(rates: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Annual energy charge with the tariff's own 700 kWh threshold, from upgrade-02 kWh."""
    joined = monthly_kwh_pair.join(rates, on="month", how="left")
    assert joined["r1"].null_count() == 0
    kwh, threshold = pl.col("kwh_after"), pl.col("threshold_kwh")
    charge = (
        pl.when(pl.col("r2").is_null())
        .then(pl.col("r1") * kwh)
        .otherwise(pl.col("r1") * pl.min_horizontal(kwh, threshold) + pl.col("r2") * (kwh - threshold).clip(lower_bound=0))
    )
    return joined.group_by("bldg_id").agg(charge.sum().alias("energy_charge"))


def bills_at_threshold(tariff: dict[str, object]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The tariff's annual energy bill with its 700 kWh threshold."""
    if tariff["includes_supply"] is None:
        return bills_rate6.select("bldg_id", "weight", BILL_COL)
    replaced = pl.col("elec_fixed_charge") + pl.col("elec_delivery_bill")
    if tariff["includes_supply"]:
        replaced = replaced + pl.col("elec_supply_bill")
    kept = bills_rate6.select("bldg_id", "weight", (pl.col(BILL_COL) - replaced).alias("kept"))
    return kept.join(energy_charge_at_threshold(tariff["rates"]), on="bldg_id").select(
        "bldg_id",
        "weight",
        (pl.col("kept") + float(tariff["fixed_monthly"]) * 12 + pl.col("energy_charge")).alias(BILL_COL),
    )


def bills_personalized(at_threshold: pl.DataFrame, tariff: dict[str, object]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The 700 kWh bill plus the personalized winter adjustment."""
    adjustment = personalized_block_adjustment(monthly_kwh_pair, tariff["rates"]).group_by("bldg_id").agg(
        pl.col("adjustment").sum()
    )
    out = at_threshold.join(adjustment, on="bldg_id", how="left")
    assert out["adjustment"].null_count() == 0
    return out.with_columns((pl.col(BILL_COL) + pl.col("adjustment")).alias(BILL_COL))
```

Rebuilding filed Rate 6 from the same monthly kWh should land on CAIRO's annual bill.
The JSON rates are rounded to five decimals, so the largest users can be off by a few
dollars. Anything much larger would mean the rebuilt variant bills are not comparable
with CAIRO's Rate 1 and Rate 6 bills.

```{python}
#| label: rebuild-check

for stem, includes_supply in [("ct_eversource_rate6", False), ("ct_eversource_rate6_supply", True)]:
    filed = load_tariff_json(STATE, UTILITY, stem, RDP_REF)
    rebuilt = bills_at_threshold(
        {
            "includes_supply": includes_supply,
            "rates": month_block_rates(filed),
            "fixed_monthly": filed["fixedchargefirstmeter"],
        }
    ).rename({BILL_COL: "rebuilt"})
    compared = rebuilt.join(bills_rate6.select("bldg_id", BILL_COL), on="bldg_id")
    error = float((compared["rebuilt"] - compared[BILL_COL]).abs().max())
    print(f"{stem}: rebuilt vs CAIRO, max abs error ${error:.2f}")
    assert error < 5
```

```{python}
#| label: build-bills

# Paul Tol's bright palette. The brand colors sit too close together for five heating types.
HEATING_COLORS = {
    "Natural gas": "#4477AA",
    "Oil/propane": "#EE6677",
    "Electric resistance": "#228833",
    "Existing heat pump": "#AA3377",
    "Other": "#66CCEE",
}


def scatter_frame(personal: pl.DataFrame, tariff: dict[str, object]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per building: bill change, pre-heat-pump kWh, heating type, in draw order."""
    winter_kwh = (
        monthly_kwh_pair.filter(pl.col("month").is_in(tariff["winter_months"]))
        .group_by("bldg_id")
        .agg(pl.col("kwh_before").sum().alias("winter_kwh"))
    )
    frame = (
        personal.select("bldg_id", "weight", pl.col("adjustment").alias("bill_change"))
        .join(baseline.select("bldg_id", "annual_kwh", "heating_label"), on="bldg_id", how="inner")
        .join(winter_kwh, on="bldg_id", how="inner")
    )
    assert frame.height == bills_rate6.height
    # Largest heating type first, so the smaller groups are drawn on top.
    draw_order = frame["heating_label"].value_counts().sort("count", descending=True)["heating_label"].to_list()
    return frame.with_columns(
        pl.col("heating_label").replace_strict({label: i for i, label in enumerate(draw_order)}).alias("_draw"),
        pl.col("heating_label").cast(pl.Enum(HEATING_ORDER)),
    ).sort("_draw")


for tariff in tariffs.values():
    tariff["at_threshold"] = bills_at_threshold(tariff)
    tariff["personalized"] = bills_personalized(tariff["at_threshold"], tariff)
    tariff["scatter"] = scatter_frame(tariff["personalized"], tariff)

pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "tariff": [t["name"] for t in tariffs.values()],
        "median_at_700": [weighted_quantile(t["at_threshold"], BILL_COL, 0.5) for t in tariffs.values()],
        "median_personalized": [weighted_quantile(t["personalized"], BILL_COL, 0.5) for t in tariffs.values()],
        "mean_change": [weighted_mean(t["personalized"], "adjustment") for t in tariffs.values()],
        "min_change": [float(t["personalized"]["adjustment"].min()) for t in tariffs.values()],
        "max_change": [float(t["personalized"]["adjustment"].max()) for t in tariffs.values()],
        "share_paying_more": [
            float(t["personalized"].filter(pl.col("adjustment") > 0)["weight"].sum() / t["personalized"]["weight"].sum())
            for t in tariffs.values()
        ],
    }
)
```

A positive change means the home pays more with the personalized threshold than with
700 kWh. That happens when its pre-heat-pump winter usage was above 700 kWh: its own
threshold is higher, so fewer kWh get the discount. A negative change means the home
used less than 700 kWh before switching, so more of its winter load gets Block 2.

```{python}
#| label: shared-axis

_all_bills = pl.concat(
    [bills_rate1.select(BILL_COL, "weight"), bills_rate6.select(BILL_COL, "weight")]
    + [t[kind].select(BILL_COL, "weight") for t in tariffs.values() for kind in ("at_threshold", "personalized")]
)
X_LIMITS = (
    weighted_quantile(_all_bills, BILL_COL, 0.01),
    weighted_quantile(_all_bills, BILL_COL, 0.99),
)
print(f"Shared x-axis: ${X_LIMITS[0]:,.0f} to ${X_LIMITS[1]:,.0f}")
```

```{python}
#| label: figure-helpers

def plot_change_scatter(key: str, x: str) -> plt.ggplot:
    """Heating-type scatter of the personalized-minus-700 kWh bill change for one tariff."""
    name = tariffs[key]["name"]
    if x == "annual_kwh":
        x_label = "Annual electricity use before the heat pump (kWh, log scale)"
        title = f"{name}: personalized vs 700 kWh, by pre-heat-pump annual use"
    else:
        x_label = "Winter electricity use before the heat pump, November–March (kWh, log scale)"
        title = f"{name}: personalized vs 700 kWh, by pre-heat-pump winter use"
    return (
        plt.ggplot(tariffs[key]["scatter"], plt.aes(x=x, y="bill_change", color="heating_label"))
        + plt.geom_hline(yintercept=0, linetype="dotted", color="gray")
        + plt.geom_point(alpha=0.75, size=1.5)
        + plt.scale_color_manual(values=HEATING_COLORS, name="Heating type")
        + plt.scale_x_log10(labels=lambda values: [f"{value:,.0f}" for value in values])
        + plt.scale_y_continuous(labels=lambda values: [f"${value:,.0f}" for value in values])
        + plt.labs(x=x_label, y="Bill change, personalized minus 700 kWh", title=title)
        + theme_switchbox()
        + plt.theme(figure_size=(10.5, 4.5))
    )


def quadrant_from_rate1(bills: pl.DataFrame, title: str):
    """Bill change from the pre-heat-pump Rate 1 bill to a post-heat-pump tariff bill, by heating type."""
    delta = (
        bills.select("bldg_id", "weight", pl.col(BILL_COL).alias("after"))
        .join(bills_rate1.select("bldg_id", pl.col(BILL_COL).alias("rate1")), on="bldg_id")
        .join(baseline.select("bldg_id", "heating_label"), on="bldg_id")
        .with_columns((pl.col("after") - pl.col("rate1")).alias("delta"))
    )
    return quadrant_by_heating(delta, "delta", title)


def quadrant_personalized(key: str):
    """Bill change from a tariff at 700 kWh to the same tariff personalized."""
    return quadrant_by_heating(
        tariffs[key]["scatter"],
        "bill_change",
        f"{tariffs[key]['name']}: personalized vs 700 kWh, by heating type",
    )
```

Each point on a scatter is one Eversource building. The y-axis is its upgrade-02 annual
bill under the personalized threshold minus its bill under the same tariff at 700 kWh:
above the dotted line the home pays more, below it the home pays less. Electricity on
the x-axis is upgrade-00 grid consumption, from before the heat pump. Color is the
home's heating type before the heat pump. On every quadrant chart, green is a lower
bill and red is a higher bill, in the same four bins used across the heat-pump reports:
$0–$1,000 and more than $1,000 in each direction. A change of exactly $0 is counted in
the $0–$1,000 loss bin.

## Rate 1 and Rate 6

Every histogram marks the weighted median with a midnight line and the weighted mean
with an orange line. The Rate 1 histogram is the pre-heat-pump bill; every other
histogram is a post-heat-pump bill.

```{python}
#| label: fig-bill-hist-rate1
#| fig-cap: "Annual energy bill of Eversource homes before switching to heat pumps, under Rate 1."

plot_annual_bill_hist(bills_rate1, "Homes before the heat pump, on Rate 1")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-bill-hist-rate6
#| fig-cap: "Annual energy bill of Eversource homes after switching to heat pumps, under Rate 6 as filed."

plot_annual_bill_hist(bills_rate6, "Heat-pump homes on Rate 6")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-quadrant-rate1-to-rate6
#| fig-cap: "Weighted share of homes, by pre-heat-pump heating type, whose annual energy bill rises or falls when they install a heat pump and move from Rate 1 to Rate 6."

quadrant_from_rate1(bills_rate6, "Bill change from Rate 1 (before heat pump) to Rate 6 (after), by heating type")
```

This change has two parts. The heat pump adds winter electricity and removes most of
the gas, oil, or propane bill, so homes that heated with delivered fuels tend to come
out ahead and homes that already heated with electricity see their electric bill grow.
On top of that, Rate 6 charges less for every kWh than Rate 1 but its customer charge
is $30.95 a month instead of $12.36, which is $223 more a year.

## Personalized Rate 6

In winter, the block boundary is each home's own upgrade-00 electricity use that month
instead of 700 kWh. kWh up to that usage pay Block 1, and only the incremental kWh
above it pay Block 2. If usage stayed the same or went down, every kWh pays Block 1.
April through October are unchanged.

```{python}
#| label: fig-bill-hist-rate6-personal
#| fig-cap: "Annual energy bill of Eversource heat-pump homes under Rate 6, with each home's winter threshold set to its own pre-heat-pump usage."

plot_annual_bill_hist(tariffs["rate6"]["personalized"], "Heat-pump homes on personalized Rate 6")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-quadrant-rate1-to-rate6-personal
#| fig-cap: "Weighted share of homes, by heating type, whose annual energy bill rises or falls when they install a heat pump and move from Rate 1 to personalized Rate 6."

quadrant_from_rate1(
    tariffs["rate6"]["personalized"],
    "Bill change from Rate 1 (before heat pump) to personalized Rate 6 (after), by heating type",
)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-bill-change-vs-annual-kwh-rate6
#| fig-cap: "Change in the annual bill from moving Rate 6's winter threshold from 700 kWh to each home's pre-heat-pump usage, against upgrade-00 annual electricity use."

plot_change_scatter("rate6", "annual_kwh")
```

## Share of incremental load under and above 700 kWh

Change `MONTHS` in the params cell to choose the months. `[1]` is January. A longer list,
such as `[11, 12, 1, 2, 3]`, averages each building's monthly shares across those months.
A month with no change in electricity use is left out of that average. The load is
ResStock's monthly `out.electricity.total.energy_consumption`, in kWh. It is the simulated
electricity use, not the scaled kWh CAIRO bills.

### Which buildings

Utility assignment lives in its own file. ResStock metadata has no utility column.

```{python}
#| label: eversource-buildings

utility_assignment = pl.read_parquet(
    RESSTOCK_ROOT / "metadata_utility" / f"state={STATE}" / "utility_assignment.parquet"
)
eversource_ids = (
    utility_assignment.filter(pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == UTILITY)
    .get_column("bldg_id")
    .to_list()
)
print(f"{len(eversource_ids):,} buildings with sb.electric_utility = {UTILITY}")
utility_assignment.filter(pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == UTILITY).head(5)
```

### Monthly electricity, before and after

Each upgrade directory holds one monthly parquet per building, named
`{bldg_id}-{upgrade}.parquet`, with one row per month.

```{python}
#| label: load-monthly

def monthly_kwh(upgrade: str, bldg_ids: list[int], months: list[int]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Monthly total electricity kWh for the requested buildings and months."""
    upgrade_int = int(upgrade)
    directory = RESSTOCK_ROOT / "load_curve_monthly" / f"state={STATE}" / f"upgrade={upgrade}"
    paths = [str(directory / f"{bldg_id}-{upgrade_int}.parquet") for bldg_id in bldg_ids]
    missing = [path for path in paths if not Path(path).exists()]
    if missing:
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"{len(missing):,} monthly files missing under {directory}, e.g. {missing[0]}"
        )
    return (
        pl.scan_parquet(paths)
        .filter(pl.col("month").is_in(months))
        .select("bldg_id", "month", pl.col(KWH_COL).alias("kwh"))
        .collect()
    )


kwh_before = monthly_kwh(UPGRADE_BEFORE, eversource_ids, MONTHS)
kwh_after = monthly_kwh(UPGRADE_AFTER, eversource_ids, MONTHS)
print(f"Upgrade {UPGRADE_BEFORE}: {kwh_before.height:,} building-months")
print(f"Upgrade {UPGRADE_AFTER}: {kwh_after.height:,} building-months")
kwh_before.head(5)
```

### Split the incremental kWh at 700

For one building-month, let $B$ be upgrade-00 kWh and $A$ be upgrade-02 kWh.
The incremental load is $A - B$. Of that increment:

- the part under the threshold is $\min(A, 700) - \min(B, 700)$
- the part above the threshold is $\max(A - 700, 0) - \max(B - 700, 0)$

Those two parts add up to $A - B$. Each share is that part divided by $A - B$.
When several months are requested, the building's result is the average of its
monthly shares. Months with $A = B$ have no incremental load, so they are dropped
from the average.

```{python}
#| label: block-shares

def incremental_block_shares(
    before: pl.DataFrame,
    after: pl.DataFrame,
    threshold_kwh: float,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Share of incremental kWh under and above `threshold_kwh`, averaged over months."""
    monthly = (
        before.rename({"kwh": "kwh_before"})
        .join(after.rename({"kwh": "kwh_after"}), on=["bldg_id", "month"], how="inner")
        .with_columns(
            (pl.col("kwh_after") - pl.col("kwh_before")).alias("incremental_kwh"),
            (
                pl.min_horizontal(pl.col("kwh_after"), threshold_kwh)
                - pl.min_horizontal(pl.col("kwh_before"), threshold_kwh)
            ).alias("incremental_kwh_under"),
            (
                (pl.col("kwh_after") - threshold_kwh).clip(lower_bound=0)
                - (pl.col("kwh_before") - threshold_kwh).clip(lower_bound=0)
            ).alias("incremental_kwh_above"),
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.when(pl.col("incremental_kwh") != 0)
            .then(pl.col("incremental_kwh_under") / pl.col("incremental_kwh"))
            .otherwise(None)
            .alias("share_under"),
            pl.when(pl.col("incremental_kwh") != 0)
            .then(pl.col("incremental_kwh_above") / pl.col("incremental_kwh"))
            .otherwise(None)
            .alias("share_above"),
        )
    )
    return monthly.group_by("bldg_id").agg(
        pl.col("share_under").mean().alias("share_under"),
        pl.col("share_above").mean().alias("share_above"),
        pl.col("incremental_kwh").sum().alias("incremental_kwh"),
        pl.col("incremental_kwh_under").sum().alias("incremental_kwh_under"),
        pl.col("incremental_kwh_above").sum().alias("incremental_kwh_above"),
        pl.col("share_under").is_not_null().sum().alias("n_months"),
    )


shares = incremental_block_shares(kwh_before, kwh_after, THRESHOLD_KWH).sort("bldg_id")
n_missing = shares.filter(pl.col("share_under").is_null()).height
print(
    f"{shares.height:,} buildings. {n_missing:,} have no electricity change "
    f"in months {MONTHS}, so their shares are null."
)
shares.head(8)
```

`share_under` and `share_above` are the result: fractions of incremental load, averaging
to the requested months. The kWh columns are the sums across those months, so you can
see the loads behind the average.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-shares

month_label = ", ".join(str(month) for month in MONTHS)
_shares_gt = (
    GT(shares.head(20), rowname_col="bldg_id")
    .fmt_percent(columns=["share_under", "share_above"], decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(
        columns=["incremental_kwh", "incremental_kwh_under", "incremental_kwh_above"],
        decimals=0,
    )
    .cols_label(
        share_under="Under 700 kWh",
        share_above="Above 700 kWh",
        incremental_kwh="Incremental kWh",
        incremental_kwh_under="kWh under",
        incremental_kwh_above="kWh above",
        n_months="Months used",
    )
    .tab_header(title=f"First 20 Eversource buildings, months {month_label}")
    .tab_options(**get_switchbox_gt_tab_options())
)
display_gt(_shares_gt)
```

A quick check that the two shares add to 1 wherever the building's electricity changed.

```{python}
#| label: sanity-check

defined = shares.filter(pl.col("share_under").is_not_null())
share_gap = (defined["share_under"] + defined["share_above"] - 1).abs().max()
kwh_gap = (
    defined["incremental_kwh_under"] + defined["incremental_kwh_above"] - defined["incremental_kwh"]
).abs().max()
print(f"Largest |share_under + share_above - 1|: {share_gap:.2e}")
print(f"Largest |kWh under + kWh above - incremental kWh|: {kwh_gap:.2e}")
print(
    defined.select(
        pl.col("share_under").mean().alias("mean_share_under"),
        pl.col("share_above").mean().alias("mean_share_above"),
        pl.col("share_under").median().alias("median_share_under"),
    )
)
```
